examples.text: Что э́то за хрень?

glosses: прост., эвф. нечто ненужное, нежелательное или низкокачественное; ерунда

examples.text: А в школу действительно не берут [домашнюю еду], не принято, в буфете можно купить, какую-нибудь хрень, вроде хуба-буба, сникерс — это еда?

Он [дом] стоял на краю буйного американского леса, ежегодно наползавшего на меня лианами и сорняками, с которыми я боролась безо всякого успеха; в мае на участке росли ландыши, расцветали ирисы, кустилась еще какая-то ботаническая хрень; летом я стригла траву газонокосилкой, осенью сгребала в кучи красные листья японского клёна, зелёные — катальпы и тёмно-лиловые — ликвидамбара; вот какие деревья росли у меня в саду.

glosses: прост., эвф. нечто непонятное или неопределённое; хреновина

examples.text: Идём обратно — что за хрень — скорость 220.

translations.source_sense_description: нечто ненужное, нежелательное или низкокачественное; ерунда

glosses: Something worthless or of poor quality; junk.

examples.text: The long-running game show went from offering good prizes to crap in no time.
The college student boasted of completing a 10,000-word essay on Shakespeare, but that claim was utter crap.
I stepped in some dog crap that was on the sidewalk.
I have to take a crap.
That soup tasted funny, and now I need to crap.

glosses: To defecate in or on (clothing etc.).

examples.text: He almost crapped his pants from fright.
Don't try to crap me: I know you're lying.
I drove an old crap car for ten years before buying a new one.

glosses: Expression of worry, fear, shock, surprise, disgust, annoyance, or dismay.

examples.text: Oh crap! The other driver's going to hit my car!
Crap! I lost the game.
What the crap?!
Aw, crap, I have to start over again from the beginning of the level.

glosses: A losing throw of 2, 3, or 12 in craps.

examples.text: To test the possibility that her husband’s luck was indestructible, Mary went to the crap tables and made a small bet.

I step up to the least-crowded crap table, taking my place to the right of a country-and-western-type stickwoman with tightly permed blond hair who looks as if she would be more comfortable dressed in the square-dance outfit of the Frontier than wearing the chinoiserie, or maybe the japonaiserie, of her purple kimono uniform.
Separately, you are playing in a crap game. The crap bets earn you $20,000 a year so long as rates stay put but could cost you a $100,000 or $200,000 loss if rates go up.

examples.text: Jetzt bin ich voll über den Scheiß hier gestolpert!
Was soll der Scheiß?

translations.source_sense_description: нечто ненужное, нежелательное или низкокачественное; ерунда
нечто ненужное, нежелательное или низкокачественное; ерунда

examples.text: Sauerkraut wird aus Kappes hergestellt.

„Erst nach einer Weile hatte ich verstanden, dass mit dem Wort Kappes die Unmengen von Kohl gemeint waren, die in diesem Wirtshaus auf großen Tellern zusammen mit dicken, schwitzenden Würsten serviert wurden.“
Red' nicht so einen Kappes.

„Anfangs hatte ich nicht verstanden, was das heißen sollte, ich hatte nur manchmal gehört, dass jemand behauptete, etwas sei Kappes, womit er doch anscheinend sagen wollte, etwas sei Unsinn oder der reine Blödsinn.“

glosses: A thing (used to refer to something vaguely or when one cannot recall or does not wish to mention its name).

examples.text: And as soon as that temperature returns to normal, let’s talk about the thingies that go through your headie at night.
What I should really do, of course, is use a Personal Digital Assistant; one of those tiny hand-held computerette thingies […]

The incorporated technology is based on absolutely serious alt-fact science—that old familiar Einsteiny, time dilation thingy only in reverse— which also forms the basis of much of LaLa Valley's tech AI prowess.
He pulled out his thingy. It was huge.

glosses: A person whose name one cannot recall.

examples.text: He reminds me of thingy from that film.

glosses: Resembling or characteristic of a thing; tangible.

examples.text: The most unpleasant, and also the thingiest, the central thing in Foreign Parts, was a giant banyan tree, putting out more and more suckers which created tangled arches, a swollen hiding-place of a tree, a series of organic traps, […]
The secret of even the thingiest SF, the most solid-walnut-to-the-knuckles fantasy, is that you don't need much to summon worlds out of air, so long as the details are the right ones.

glosses: jemand oder etwas, dessen Namen der sprechenden Person gerade nicht einfällt oder dessen Namen die sprechende Person nicht kennt

examples.text: Was macht denn der Dingsbums da? Wie heißt er noch?
„Das hat die Dingsbums zu mir gesagt.“ —„ Wer ist denn Dingsbums?“ — „Na du weißt schon: lange, blonde Haare, die Nase mitten im Gesicht… Dingsbums halt!“
